audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL state management (EIP-161 empty account cleanup, account creation nonce), EL EVM mechanics (EIP-8024 extended stack manipulation opcodes), EL networking (EIP-2364 eth/64 forkid handshake, EIP-778 ENR records), EL signing standards (EIP-712 typed data signing), EL fork transitions (EIP-606 Homestead), and CL topics (Capella validator withdrawals, Electra fork state transition, Electra light client fork upgrade). Also includes EIP-4 governance classification.

in_scope: State Transition (EIP-161 account cleanup, nonce increment)
P2P Networking (EIP-2364 eth/64 forkid, EIP-778 ENR)
Gas Economics (EIP-161 dead account gas charge)
Validator Operations (Capella block proposal with withdrawals, BLS credential changes)
Fork Transitions (Electra beacon state upgrade, deposit queue migration)
Light Client (Electra LC fork upgrade, merkle branch normalization)

threats: Trick users into signing malicious typed data via EIP-712
Signature replay across domains if chainId omitted
Obfuscated message content in wallet display

el_vectors.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p eth/64 handshake, ENR exchange)
threats: Lie about forkid to waste connection slots
Eclipse attacks via false ENR records
Send invalid blocks for wrong fork rules

cl_vectors.entry_point: P2P Network (beacon block proposal, BLS credential change gossip)
threats: Omit or alter withdrawals in proposed blocks
Exploit deposit queue migration edge cases during Electra fork
Serve pre-fork light client data with incorrect format during Electra transition
Provide stale or corrupted merkle branches

misclassified_entities.reason: EIP-4 governance entity, not a runtime data source. EIP authors participate in a social/governance process, not a protocol-level trust boundary.
Governance entity, not a runtime external entity. Core developers implement consensus changes but do not interact with the system at runtime.
System administrator controlling the node. Trusted setup entity, not a runtime trust boundary. Similar to EXT-OPERATOR in previous batches.

Trusted entity controlling the validator. While they submit BLS credential changes, they are the authorized controller, not an external threat. However, the BLS credential change message itself crosses a trust boundary when submitted to the network.
Wallet user who approves/rejects signing. This is the human-in-the-loop trust model element, not a protocol-level external entity. The user's decisions are mediated by the wallet UI.
Internal EVM component (smart contract verifying signatures on-chain). Not external to the system boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via eth_signTypedData RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps submit structured typed data for signing via EIP-712. Any web application can request signatures. The typed data content could be malicious, misleading, or designed for replay attacks. The wallet must display data accurately and the user must approve.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p eth/64 Handshake
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p TCP (eth/64 Status message with forkid)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers in the P2P network are unauthenticated. They provide forkid in Status messages which must be validated against local fork configuration. Malicious peers can lie about fork state to waste connection slots or attempt eclipse attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate blocks that must be validated against the correct fork rules (Frontier, Homestead, etc.) based on block height. Invalid blocks from wrong fork epoch must be rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via ENR Exchange
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers provide ENR records that must be cryptographically validated: size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP structure, sorted unique keys, valid secp256k1 signature. Even with valid signatures, connectivity information (IP/port) could be stale or intentionally misleading.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Discovery Service
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DNS infrastructure providing ENR records for node discovery. Subject to DNS spoofing/hijacking. ENR signatures limit the impact to DoS (directing to wrong IPs) but cannot prevent connectivity disruption.

trusted_external_entities.name: ENS Registry for ENR Resolution
trusted_external_entities.rationale: ENS-based ENR discovery depends on on-chain data integrity. While on-chain data is harder to tamper with, the resolver path may introduce vulnerabilities. ENR signatures provide cryptographic binding regardless.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker Replaying EIP-712 Signatures
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker who captures valid EIP-712 signatures can attempt replay attacks. Domain separator provides cross-contract/cross-chain protection, but same-domain replay requires application-level nonce tracking (not part of EIP-712 standard).

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates withdrawals to the EL execution engine via Engine API (JWT-authenticated). The EL must validate that the execution payload it produces matches the specified withdrawals. Authenticated channel but content requires validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peers Serving Light Client Data
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network (light client update messages in pre-fork format)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: During the Electra fork transition, peers may serve light client data in pre-fork (Deneb) format. This data must be locally upgraded using upgrade functions and validated cryptographically. Merkle branches must be normalized to Electra depth.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Wallet must faithfully display typed data to user. Domain separator must include chainId and verifyingContract. User must approve signing. Application-level replay protection (nonces) is NOT provided by EIP-712 and must be implemented separately.

ForkID must be validated per EIP-2124: compute local forkHash from genesis + fork blocks, compare with remote. Incompatible peers must be disconnected immediately. Peers may lie about forkid to waste connection slots.
Blocks must be validated against the correct fork rules based on block height. Fork-specific validation (Frontier vs Homestead vs later) must be applied correctly. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

ENR validation: size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP, sorted unique keys, valid secp256k1 signature over keccak256 of content. Sequence number must be checked for freshness. Unknown identity schemes must be rejected.

ENR records from DNS must pass full cryptographic validation. DNS responses themselves are untrusted (potential spoofing). DNSSEC provides additional protection but is not required. Impact of DNS spoofing limited to DoS due to ENR signature verification.

ENR records from ENS must pass full cryptographic validation. On-chain data integrity depends on Ethereum consensus. Resolver contracts could be compromised. ENR signature verification provides final trust anchor.

Domain separator prevents cross-contract and cross-chain replay. Same-domain replay prevention requires application-level nonce tracking. Verifying contracts must correctly implement EIP-712 encoding and check domain separator fields.

JWT-authenticated channel. EL must produce execution payloads that include exactly the specified withdrawals. Content validation: withdrawal amounts, validator indices, and execution addresses must match CL state. A malicious CL could specify incorrect withdrawals.

Pre-fork (Deneb) format data must be locally upgraded to Electra format using upgrade functions. Merkle branches must be normalized using Electra generalized indices. All cryptographic verification (sync committee signatures) must pass after format conversion.
